title: We have two engines and only one of them works, and we admit it.
hook: We have two execution engines. One works. The other is a museum piece. Here is the honest tour.
thesis: The idealized ORCA ExecutionEngine (fourteen modules) is initialized at gateway boot but orphaned by explicit decision: its only worker port has a null executor, dispatch never calls execute, and it emits events on a private queue nothing consumes. The live business path is the PING event spine. Admitting this publicly is trust-building content: building in public means naming the parts that are not finished yet. This post walks the difference between the two, in the falsifiable format.

verified: The idealized engine is initialized but orphaned by explicit decision: null executor, dispatch never calls execute, private queue with no consumer (orca-omniroute-audit 2026-09-13 sections 2, 7, 8, via SYSTEMS.md section 4).

The live path is the PING spine: Postgres-backed event spine feeds an event-to-mission bridge (28 event types), MissionRuntime, scheduler, WorkerRuntime dispatch by exact event-type match (audit sections 2, 5, 6).

approval_gate: Nolan approves every exact post. Silence is not approval.
